description: Zhaiyu Chen at Technical University of Munich publishes the PolyGNN Munich Data benchmark for reconstructing three-dimensional buildings from point clouds. Zenodo metadata links the dataset to the PolyGNN research method and states that its meshes derive from Bavarian Open GeoData LoD2 models. The native TUM2TWIN documentation describes simulated airborne laser scanning with HELIOS++, including sensor geometry, noise and occlusion. It reports 281,571 buildings and approximately 6.5 billion points, with 10,000 buildings for evaluation. These are provider metadata, not independently reproduced counts. Coverage is Munich, Germany, with city-building geometry represented through synthetic observations. The selected Zenodo dataset was published on 1 December 2024 with open access and CC BY 4.0. Access is free; individual file formats were not established in the reviewed registry projection. Caveats include synthetic sampling and the detail limits inherited from LoD2 source models. It supports evaluation of building geometry used in digital environments and relates to the aggregate TUM2TWIN benchmark. No benchmark archive or code file was obtained.
